challenges: ‘No sprint’/slow speed runs feel manageable here — practice line-of-sight breaks around the kitchen island.
insanityTips: Use sound cues: with limited evidence, listen for double-steps vs normal pacing during hunts.
If you can’t confirm orbs, keep an eye on hallway corners — orbs can be easy to miss in small rooms.
Bring a motion sensor early; tiny map means one sensor can cover multiple rooms.
name: 6 Tanglewood Drive
nightmareTips: Sprint the first sweep: kitchen → garage → living room is the fastest ‘power search’ route.
If the ghost is in the basement, stage gear at the stairs to reduce back-and-forth.
Listen for step sounds: the hallway is short, so footsteps + door touches narrow location fast.
summary: A tight starter house with quick routes between rooms. Great for fast evidence runs and learning early hunt behavior.
tips: Keep the fuse box on early and keep lights on near the ghost room to stabilise sanity.
Use the central hallway as your main 'spine' for quick sweeps with EMF and UV.

challenges: Try a ‘stairs-only’ gear rule: everything staged at the stairs forces clean search discipline.
insanityTips: If evidence is scarce, use hunt pathing: Edgefield’s long corridors make speed tells easier to spot.
Keep lights on in your search path to slow sanity drain while you narrow the favourite room.
Use salt + UV in choke points (stairs landing / hallway) to confirm footprints quickly.
name: 42 Edgefield Road
nightmareTips: Treat it like two halves: clear downstairs quickly, then commit upstairs rather than bouncing.
The long upstairs hallway is dangerous in hunts — pre-plan a closet/hide route.
Stage extra gear at the bottom of the stairs to keep trips efficient.
summary: A narrow house with a basement. Hallways get congested but you're rarely far from a door or room to duck into.
tips: Use sound sensors to watch for movement between floors if the ghost feels like it’s roaming.
During hunts, break line-of-sight quickly by cutting into a nearby room rather than committing to long hallways.

challenges: ‘One floor at a time’ runs: you may only bring gear upstairs after confirming downstairs is cold-free.
insanityTips: Use line-of-sight breaks: the living area is open, so identify safe corners before provoking hunts.
If freezing is unclear, check adjacent rooms — Ridgeview’s airflow makes temps ‘feel’ wider.
Keep a crucifix near stair approaches if you’re unsure where the ghost roams.
name: 10 Ridgeview Court
nightmareTips: Prioritise the open-plan living/dining/kitchen first — activity spreads and can mislead you.
If the ghost is upstairs, keep one person watching stair audio/steps to avoid surprise hunts.
Garage ghosts are common pain: temperature + sound usually locates faster than running room-to-room.
summary: A more open small house with a basement. You get decent sightlines, but hunts can still catch you mid-staircase.
tips: If the ghost room is upstairs, set a camera on the landing so you can confirm DOTS / orbs quickly.
Use the basement stairs as a predictable route: plan your escape before you commit to evidence setup.

challenges: Practice ‘speed locate’: first 2 minutes you only carry thermo + EMF, nothing else.
insanityTips: Use audio: Willow has clear door-touch sound; use it to triangulate upstairs rooms.
Set up DOTS acrosss doorways; narrow bedrooms mean DOTS coverage is efficient.
If you suspect a roaming ghost, track where it interacts rather than where it hunts.
name: 13 Willow Street
nightmareTips: The basement can waste time — only commit once you’ve checked power + listened for interactions.
The upstairs rooms are tight: a single motion sensor can cover multiple doors.
If you get early EMF in the garage, check adjacent storage quickly before assuming garage room.
summary: A small house with a larger, more usable basement than most. Good for practising evidence setups and looping routes.
tips: Basement ghosts can be fast to confirm with temps; keep a thermometer or temp-reading device on hand early.
Use the garage/utility areas as staging spots to avoid cluttering the ghost room.

challenges: Try a ‘no attic until found’ rule — it stops the attic from eating your early sanity.
insanityTips: If evidence is limited, watch for mannequin/doll interactions in the work/child rooms — they’re strong tells.
Use sound sensors (if enabled) or careful listening: farmhouse creaks can hide footsteps.
Place salt at stair choke points to confirm wander patterns.
name: Grafton Farmhouse
nightmareTips: The foyer light is unreliable — bring a flashlight and avoid trusting the main light during hunts.
Attic/upper rooms can drain sanity fast; keep an eye on teammates when searching upstairs.
Stage gear in the foyer: every path routes through it, so it’s a perfect ‘hub’.
summary: A farmhouse with a strong mood and a few awkward corners. Staircases and long lines of sight are the danger points.
tips: Farmhouses punish over-roaming: confirm the ghost room before you scatter equipment everywhere.
Set a safe hiding plan near each staircase so you’re not caught sprinting acrosss open rooms.

challenges: Fast-food panic: complete 2 objectives before confirming the ghost type.
No hiding: practise breaking line-of-sight and using furniture as cover instead of dedicated hiding spots.
insanityTips: Treat evidence as secondary; confirm with hunts, footsteps, and interaction patterns.
Keep the lights plan simple: one lit route for sanity, one dark route for hiding.
Mark hiding spots early so you can test speed/line of sight safely.
name: Nell's Diner
nightmareTips: Prioritise behaviour tells early: speed changes, hunt timing, and room roaming.
Place motion + sound sensors along the main route to confirm where activity is moving.
Use a safe loop (kitchen/island or hallway corners) before you risk cursed items.
summary: A compact, cluttered diner. Evidence can be quick, but hunts feel claustrophobic because the space is tight and noisy.
tips: Use the truck cameras early if you suspect orbs or DOTS to avoid crowding the dining area.
Be careful with sound: small maps can mask ghost steps and object throws behind ambient noise.

challenges: Time attack: identify ghost within 5 minutes — this map is perfect practice.
insanityTips: Use footsteps on gravel/wood to help identify approach direction during hunts.
If you can’t lock evidence, use hunting speed tells — Woodwind makes them very obvious.
Don’t over-commit to one ‘cold spot’ — outdoor temps can feel weird; confirm with interactions.
name: Camp Woodwind
nightmareTips: Treat it like a loop: sweep tent → picnic → firepit and you’ll find activity fast.
Hunts are line-of-sight heavy outdoors — break sight with props and keep moving.
Keep gear tight: you can carry less because distances are short.
summary: An ultra-compact outdoor map. The ghost feels close at all times, so movement and line-of-sight matter more than distance.
tips: Keep your escape route in mind before you start a trigger-heavy objective (like photo runs).
Use a strong flashlight and stick to a consistent lap around the main tent area to track activity.

challenges: ‘One-smudge’ runs: you only get one smudge per player — forces better escape planning.
insanityTips: Use the narrow rooms to your advantage: DOTS + motion sensors cover lots of space with few placements.
If you’re unsure on evidence, trigger a safe hunt and read speed changes on stairs/hallways.
Keep a smudge in hand on attic investigations — it can trap you otherwise.
name: Bleasdale Farmhouse
nightmareTips: Bleasdale is vertical: confirm ground floor before committing to upstairs + attic.
The long central stairs are risky in hunts — know your nearest hiding spot before provoking.
If the ghost is in the attic, stage gear at the top landing and keep exits clear.
summary: A bigger farmhouse with multiple useful outdoor areas. Great for learning longer rotations, but it’s easy to waste time roaming.
tips: Pick a staging room close to the ghost room so you’re not hauling equipment acrosss the entire house.
If the ghost is upstairs, put salt/UV at the top of the stairs to collect evidence during early activity.

challenges: ‘One-wing only’ runs: you must identify ghost without entering the other cell block.
insanityTips: Hunts can be long: pre-plan a loop route around corners and avoid dead-end cells.
If evidence is scarce, use sound + motion sensors in hallways to track roam paths.
Keep sanity management tight — prison distance makes recovery trips expensive.
name: Prison
nightmareTips: Pick a wing and commit — prison wastes time if you bounce between blocks.
Stage gear in the central hall so you can pivot without returning to the truck.
Listen for cell door touches: they narrow location faster than random room checks.
summary: A huge open interior split into wings. Long sightlines are dangerous, and evidence collection can be slow if you don't narrow the area fast.
tips: Use sound sensors and motion sensors to isolate the wing before you start placing everything.
Keep a safe room in mind near each wing entrance; committing deep into cell blocks can trap you.

challenges: ‘No cabin’ challenge: you can’t hide in the cabin — forces outdoor escape planning.
insanityTips: Use the cabin as a safe ‘reset’ point — set crucifix/smudges there to stabilise hunts.
When evidence is limited, rely on hunt speed and sanity thresholds; this map gives long chase lanes.
Use motion sensors along main paths to track roam direction.
name: Maple Lodge Campsite
nightmareTips: Split the map: cabin + dock area vs tents + firepit — clear one side fully before swapping.
Sound carries weird outdoors; confirm room with multiple interactions before committing gear.
Stage gear at the entrance path to cut long runs to the truck.
summary: An outdoor map with wide spaces and low cover. Weather and visibility matter, and hunts can be brutal if you misread distance.
tips: Use the truck to confirm orbs/DOTS where possible; outdoor visibility can be inconsistent.
Place crucifixes earlier than you think — it’s easy to be too far away when a hunt starts.

challenges: ‘Top-down’ search: you start at the top floor and work down, staging gear as you go.
insanityTips: With limited evidence, watch hunt pathing: tight stairs make speed/tell reading easier.
Keep smudge + lighter ready before going above mid floors — escapes are limited.
Use motion sensors on stair landings to track travel direction.
name: Point Hope
nightmareTips: Vertical map: stage gear on mid-floors so you don’t stair-run to the truck.
Narrow stairwells are risky in hunts — pick a ‘safe floor’ and retreat early.
Use sound cues: footsteps and door touches are easier to pinpoint than temps in a tall building.
summary: A tall, narrow lighthouse. Escape routes are linear and tight, so planning matters more than raw speed.
tips: Treat each floor as a checkpoint: identify where you can safely reset during a hunt.
Drop a spare flashlight or smudge on a mid-floor so you’re never empty-handed if you get trapped above.

challenges: ‘No sprint’ hunt practice: high school corridors teach line-of-sight discipline.
insanityTips: If evidence is limited, provoke a controlled hunt and read speed in the long corridors.
Keep lights on in your travel path; sanity drains fast on large maps.
Place motion sensors at major intersections to catch roam direction.
name: Brownstone High School
nightmareTips: Drop a ‘gear pile’ near the closest entrance; the walk to truck is brutal otherwise.
Use sound + thermo to find the wing first; room-by-room is too slow.
Hallways aren’t ghost rooms — focus on classrooms/bathrooms and listen for door touches.
summary: A massive, echoing school with long corridors. Finding the ghost room is the real fight — evidence comes later.
tips: Use parabolic microphone and sound sensors to locate activity before you commit gear.
Keep the team spaced: too many people in one hallway wastes time and increases confusion during hunts.

challenges: ‘Wing lock’ runs: you may only investigate one wing for the entire contract.
insanityTips: With limited evidence, hunts are your best ‘data’ — Sunny Meadows gives long corridors for speed tells.
Don’t chase interactions acrosss floors; track consistent activity to avoid being baited by roaming.
Smudges are mandatory: plan a chain of safe rooms to rotate through.
name: Sunny Meadows Mental Institution
nightmareTips: Treat it as zones: only open the wing you intend to play to reduce search overwhelm.
Stage gear at the entrance of your chosen wing, not at the truck.
Use parabolic/audio to find the wing quickly before doing any detailed room checks.
summary: The biggest and most punishing location. Navigation, sound, and time management matter as much as evidence.
tips: Mark your path mentally: it’s easy to lose orientation in long corridors and repeated rooms.
Commit to one wing at a time. Roaming acrosss wings early is the fastest way to waste 20 minutes.

challenges: Restricted rush: get first evidence within 3 minutes.
No truck: play as if you can't use the truck monitors for confirmations.
insanityTips: Bring sensors first so you can reduce guesswork when evidence is limited.
Test one behaviour at a time (speed, LOS, special tells) so you don't mix signals.
Keep comms clean: call out room changes and hunt starts immediately.
name: Sunny Meadows Mental Institution (Restricted)
nightmareTips: Split jobs: one person finds the room, one sets sensors to track roaming and hunts.
Use sound sensors to identify the active wing/area before committing gear.
Plan a retreat route from the ghost room to a confirmed hiding spot.
summary: A smaller variant of Sunny Meadows with a single wing layout. It keeps the vibe, but cuts down the time sink — still dangerous if you wander.
tips: Treat it like a medium map: isolate the wing quickly and set up a single staging point.
Don’t over-extend: restricted layouts punish chasing noises into long dead ends.
